# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [yellow] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[0] 2:[4] 3:[1] 4:[7] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[purple] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 ✍ 👍]

The bomb shows a blue light, display value 6, a red-yellow-red painted strip, keypad labels 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7 with nothing entered, and six wires colored red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. I am telling both teammates the complete visible state so Mute can match it to the manual and Blind knows what physical modules to expect.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Visible state: display 6; light blue; painted strip red yellow red; keypad engraved 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, one digit, nothing entered; wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. Please read the manual and tell Blind the required actions.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state: display 6; light blue; painted strip red yellow red; keypad labels 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, one digit, nothing entered; wires in order red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. Mute is consulting the manual for the procedure.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [yellow] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[0] 2:[4] 3:[1] 4:[7] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[purple] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👍]

The display has changed from 6 to 0 while all other visible features remain the same. I cannot interpret the mute’s gestures reliably without an agreed code, so I will establish a yes/no response and ask Mute to provide the manual’s instructions for Blind. Blind needs the updated display value.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gestures, but their meaning is unclear. Please use 👍 for yes and 👎 for no. Does the manual give a required action for this bomb? Then send the required wire, keypad, or other instructions using an agreed gesture code or by answering my questions.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: the display now reads 0. Light remains blue; strip remains red yellow red; keypad is 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7 with one digit and nothing entered; wires remain red blue yellow green purple orange. I am obtaining the manual instructions from Mute and will relay them.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [yellow] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[0] 2:[4] 3:[1] 4:[7] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[purple] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆]

The bomb now shows display 6 and a yellow light; the strip, keypad, and wires are unchanged. Mute confirmed “yes” with the agreed thumbs-up, and then sent six upward-pointing gestures. I will treat that as the number 6 for now, but it does not yet identify an operation. I am asking whether the manual’s required action concerns cutting a wire, and I will relay the current visual state to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 6; light yellow; strip red yellow red; keypad 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, one digit, nothing entered; wires red, blue, yellow, green, purple, orange. Mute confirmed the manual requires an action and sent six upward gestures, apparently indicating 6, but the operation is not yet clear.")
speak(to="mute", text="Does the manual require cutting a wire? Answer with 👍 for yes or 👎 for no. If yes, send the wire number as that many 👆 gestures; if no, I will ask about the keypad.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [red] [yellow] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[0] 2:[4] 3:[1] 4:[7] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[purple] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆]

The display and light have changed again, now reading 2 with a green light; the strip, keypad, and wire colors are unchanged. Mute again sent thumbs-up followed by six upward gestures in response to the wire-cut question, so the safest interpretation is: yes, cut wire 6. I am relaying that exact instruction to Blind and asking Mute to confirm the interpretation.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Instruction from Mute: cut wire 6. The wires are 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. Current display is 2 and light is green; strip is red yellow red; keypad labels are 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7.")
speak(to="mute", text="I am interpreting your 👍 followed by six 👆 gestures as: yes, cut wire 6. Confirm this exact instruction with 👍, or correct it with 👎.")
```
